gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Dabbsson 2000L, its 'best value' pick, burns about 26 W with the AC inverter on and nothing plugged in, about 624 Wh a day, or roughly 30% of its 2,048 Wh. TheSolarLab measured the Anker SOLIX S2000 at about 6 W (about 144 Wh a day) and the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at about 17 W.
standout_why: I opened four of the cited pages. powerstations.reviews/prices gives rated Wh and price only, with no measurements. outagereadyhq says it never used the units and has no measurements. gearjunkie gives one measured figure in this class: about 6 W idle and 34 h of fridge runtime for the S2000, with nothing for the Dabbsson, Pecron, Bluetti, EcoFlow or Jackery. wattpowerstation gives tested usable Wh (Dabbsson 2000L 1,887 Wh, Pecron 75%, Elite 200 V2 1,989 Wh, C2000 Gen 2 1,818 Wh, Explorer 2000 v2 1,773 Wh) but does not name the testers and gives no idle draw. None of these pages has an idle-draw figure for the Dabbsson 2000L, Pecron E2400LFP, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max, Jackery or C2000 Gen 2. None gives Notebookcheck's named S2000 figures (1,900+ Wh at 250 W, about 78% round trip). Popular Mechanics (cited) would not load, so I could not check its 92% Elite 200 V2 figure.
decides: ChatGPT ranked the Dabbsson 2000L first on price per usable Wh at full-load discharge. For outage use with small, steady loads like a fridge, router or CPAP, the inverter's no-load draw matters a lot. In TheSolarLab's tests the Dabbsson (26 W) and DELTA 3 Max (27 W) lose 600+ Wh a day to overhead, against about 144 Wh for the S2000 (6 W). That makes the S2000 the better outage buy despite costing about $51 more. The Pecron E2400LFP is the same price as the Dabbsson but idles lower (13.6 W). It also posted only 75% AC efficiency at 2,275 W, so it is a poor pick for heavy loads. The Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (17 W, 90%) and C2000 Gen 2 (about 18 W, about 89%) sit in between. The Dabbsson remains the pick for short, high-wattage use, where its 93% inverter efficiency matters more than idle draw.

findings.label: Idle consumption, AC inverter on, no load
findings.note: Measured by TheSolarLab. The page shows no review date or author. 26 W × 24 h = 624 Wh/day, about 30% of 2,048 Wh.

findings.label: AC inverter efficiency
findings.note: TheSolarLab tested 'a variety of different loads' without naming them. It reports an AC charge time of 'under two hours' and no noise figure in dB.

findings.label: Idle consumption, AC inverter on / off
findings.note: Measured by TheSolarLab; the page shows no review date. 6 W × 24 h = 144 Wh/day, about 7% of 2,010 Wh. GearJunkie (cited by ChatGPT) also reports about 6 W.

findings.label: AC efficiency; AC charge time 0–100%
findings.note: TheSolarLab calls it among the most efficient units it has tested. It also reports about 5 h to full on 400 W of solar in ideal conditions.

findings.label: Usable AC capacity at about 250 W continuous
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Marcus Schwarten, 2026-10-07)
findings.note: Notebookcheck tested the EU 230 V unit, rated 2,000 Wh; the US unit is rated 2,010 Wh. Charging drew just over 2,400 Wh from the wall at about 1,100 W, about 82% charge efficiency, about 78% round trip. Idle with AC on cost just over 10% of the battery per 24 h, about 200 Wh/day, higher than TheSolarLab's 6 W. Bypass/UPS draw was about 3 W and charging noise about 35 dB.

findings.label: Idle (AC on); AC efficiency; AC charge 0–100%
findings.note: Measured by TheSolarLab; the page shows no review date. 27 W × 24 h = 648 Wh/day. Solar took just over 4 h to full on 500 W of input.

findings.label: Idle (AC on); AC efficiency
findings.note: 17 W × 24 h = 408 Wh/day. TheSolarLab saw AC input hover around 1,300 W unless Emergency Charging Mode was on, which raises it to 1,800 W.

findings.label: Idle (AC outlets on); AC efficiency; AC charge 0–100%
findings.source_title: TheSolarLab: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 review
findings.note: Anker advertises 9 W idle; TheSolarLab found 9 W only with the screen and USB on, and about 18 W with the AC outlets on standby.

findings.label: Usable AC capacity at about 200 W / at 1,800 W
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck: Anker Solix C2000 Gen 2 review (Marcus Schwarten, published 2026-02-24, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Notebookcheck tested the EU version. Charging drew almost 2,350 Wh from the wall, about 87% charge efficiency. Noise was about 35 dB at 1 m under high load. Usable energy at low load was well below usable energy at high load.

findings.label: AC efficiency at 2,275 W; idle (AC on)
findings.note: The first run shut off after 36 minutes, against about 54 expected, with about 15% left. The retest after Pecron's recalibration gave 75%. In the idle test the battery fell from 98% to 82% in 24 h, about 327 Wh. AC charge took about 1 h 21 min. wattpowerstation's unnamed 75% figure matches this.

findings.label: Measured discharge energy
findings.source_title: StorageReview: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 review (Dylan Dougherty, 2025-04-25)
findings.note: StorageReview does not state the discharge load. Recharging used 2.44 kWh, so round trip is 1.91 ÷ 2.44 ≈ 78% (my arithmetic). No idle wattage is reported.
